title: Depreciation declares the schedule and rounding boundary
question: Straight-line, fixed declining and sum-of-years methods are alternatives; cost/salvage/life/partial-year bounds remain financial policy.

evidence.title: Depreciation methods choose different schedules and rounding boundaries
explanation: Fixed declining, straight-line and SYD depreciation select different period schedules; fixed declining rounds its intermediate rate to three places and prorates first/extra years.
The fixed-declining loop and distinct closed formulas support separate candidate schedules. None supplies a universal salvage floor or accounting-policy selection.

Cost/lifetime/period/month arguments satisfying the actual method-specific guards; zero cost/life are not uniformly excluded. A period beyond life can continue through the loop, and zero lifetime remains admitted. Source behavior is not a statutory depreciation rule. No upstream execution. evidence.title: Depreciation declares salvage clipping and the schedule observation
explanation: Straight-line returns one annual cost-minus-salvage amount; double-declining returns a period matrix, clips a period to salvage, and leaves preallocated later entries zero after breaking.
The loop uses the remaining book value and stops after a clipped period. That output differs from a single-period observation and does not implement an automatic straight-line switch.

Double-declining t>=2 plus intended integral period count; cost/salvage economic admission remains caller policy. Salvage above cost and fractional/zero lifetime are not uniformly validated. evidence.title: Depreciation permits zero lifetime and continuation beyond economic bounds
explanation: The depreciation functions lack common economic admission and terminal/salvage controls: zero lifetime is admitted and fixed-declining periods can extend beyond life.
The guards and loop bounds expose policy gaps, but a source library formula alone does not select the correct accounting or tax regime.
